severityMeaning.P1: Blocks dense-workspace visual acceptance or requires an explicit design decision
severityMeaning.P2: Visible adaptation or consistency question to resolve before final fidelity acceptance

items.title: Expanded chrome consumes the working area
items.evidence: 1440×900, XL / text 150% / X24 / Y12: header 266px, banner 102px, first card y588. Header commands wrap over multiple rows; account and notification also separate. documentOverflow=0 does not describe this loss of working area.
items.next: Use the existing TopBar/DropdownMenu primitives to define an overflow recipe: keep the primary command and move secondary commands into a named keyboard-accessible menu. Keep account/notification controls in a coherent compact header.
items.exit: All original commands remain available by keyboard, focus/draft survive resize, header height follows a single control row plus host spacing at stress settings. Compare before/after visually; do not hide commands or shrink inherited typography.

items.title: Chrome surfaces have no accepted mapping to the reference
items.evidence: Figma header/sidebar/card summary #2c2c2c; actual canonical Dark header/sidebar/card rgb(23,23,24). Passive main area uses container/neutral/default (rgba white 0.11) over the base. Card/default border rgba white 0.11 also differs from source #444 at 0.667px.
items.next: Define surface/page/base/subtle/raised usage for application chrome and compare the actual hierarchy in both themes. Preserve owner token overrides and shared SEDA roles; do not paste source hex into local component overrides.
items.exit: An explicit agreed role mapping and screenshots establish which differences are deliberate. A source screenshot or token existence alone does not accept the mapping.

items.title: Readable SEDA typography changes source density and hierarchy
items.evidence: Source navigation/tabs/card title are 11px; source header title is 13px regular. Actual M is 14px controls/title, card title 14px/600 and metadata 12px. Long Sidebar labels wrap by documented SEDA policy, giving 48px rows where the source uses 32px single-line rows.
items.next: Agree application density and typography roles; preserve the owner's 14px portal-shell decision. Review an explicit compact application profile or role composition rather than adding arbitrary nested font-size/ellipsis overrides.
items.exit: The chosen density, long-label policy and readable hierarchy are accepted in the source comparison and both themes. Current wrap behavior is not mislabeled a Sidebar implementation bug.

items.title: Grid spacing and card shape differ from the frame
items.evidence: Dark M: first card x265/w367.66/h271.69/r8, source x275/w355.67/h259/r13. Effective grid gutter 24 vs source 34; grid gap 24 vs source 32. Card summary uses 12px inline padding and 8px gap vs source 16px and 12px.
items.next: Record one spacing/card recipe and its intentional adaptation. Keep external spacing independent of text scale as previously agreed. If a source-fidelity configuration is needed, use supported foundation values and shared composition rules.
items.exit: One approved recipe explains the differences; no silent replacement of the reference or CSS patch on every application.

items.title: Content icon and typography sizing need an explicit relationship
items.evidence: Card title remains 14px across S/M/L/XL while its file-type glyph box changes 14/16/18/20px; at XL×150% title is 21px and glyph 30px. Avatar remains 24px. The text-scale path works; the separate density/identity sizing choices are not yet accepted as a content-slot rule.
items.next: Define content glyph, identity avatar and control icon roles separately. Inspect optical ink, baseline and line-height; do not infer a defect solely from different numerical sizes or recolor identity artwork.
items.exit: The relationship is documented and visually checked at baseline/extremes; shared component/recipe ownership is explicit.

items.owner: public Card/Avatar integration and composition contracts
items.title: Files still uses local card/avatar compositions
items.evidence: recents.tsx renders article/button/summary and image avatars directly; its imports do not include public Card or Avatar. Both public modules now exist, but their contracts and the media + open + selection + menu composition need review. This is not proof that the public Card implementation is broken.
items.next: Check the actual public API against Files anatomy. Reuse compatible public components; where it cannot express the composition, document and solve the shared API/recipe gap instead of adding another local visual copy.
items.exit: Imports, runtime anatomy, token provenance, native interaction semantics and visual states agree; a module count is not used as evidence of integration.

items.title: Extra navigation and local-data footer shift the source hierarchy
items.evidence: Current Files adds a Notifications destination and a local-data footer not present in frame 1:691. The source has the notification bell; the additional row and larger type change the Starred start and visible project density.
items.next: Record whether both notification entry points and the persistent footer are intentional for this application. Preserve working features while reviewing their placement; do not remove them just to lower screenshot difference.
items.exit: Navigation composition is explicitly accepted, with matching screenshots and accessible destinations.
